ov: A shy, spiral-horned antelope of southeast Africa, and the most sexually dimorphic antelope: males are slate grey with a shaggy fringe and horns, while females are small, hornless and rusty brown with white stripes. It keeps to thickets near water.

why.et: Hunted as game; big-horned males are prized by sport hunters.

ht: Males up to 110 cm; females up to 90 cm at the shoulder
rg: Southeast Africa, from southern Malawi through Mozambique and Zimbabwe to eastern South Africa and Eswatini.
df: Leaves, fruit, flowers and twigs, and fresh grass in the rainy season. It needs regular water.
fx: Uses a sharp, dog-like bark to warn others of danger, and reacts to the alarm calls of impala, baboons and kudu.
Hairy glands on its feet leave its scent wherever it walks.
